narrative: Material PL3__M5BF99BE shows erratic daily demand (CV=0.67) with a statistically significant downward trend (slope=-0.58 units/day, p<0.0001) over the March 2025 to March 2026 observation window. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.79, mean=1.18 days), necessitating a robust safety stock of 518 units to achieve the 95% service level target. The economically optimal order quantity of 2,122 units is constrained by the 1,871.6-unit storage limit to 1,353 units, yielding a total annual cost of $5,197 versus $15,350 under the current SAP policy.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic demand (CV=0.67) with high non-zero fraction (92.5%) and unstable lead times favours a continuous-review (r,Q) policy over periodic review. The policy triggers a fixed replenishment of Q=1353 units whenever on-hand inventory falls to the reorder point r=777, providing responsive coverage against both demand and lead-time variability without the latency of periodic review.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is binding: the unconstrained EOQ (2,122 units) exceeds available space after safety stock (1,871 - 518 = 1,353 units). The capacity cap increases annual ordering frequency from ~25 to ~40 orders and raises ordering cost accordingly. If storage capacity is expanded, the EOQ-optimal policy would reduce total costs further. The downward demand trend may also erode the accuracy of the current safety stock over time.
